## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

browser-use <<'PY'

#!/bin/bash
# Walk DEV repos: classify, fetch, report one line each.
DEV="$HOME/DEV"
OUT="/Users/kristinarash/.claude/jobs/2112ee97/tmp/inventory.txt"
: > "$OUT"

candidates=()
for d in "$DEV"/*/ "$DEV"/Football/*/ "$DEV"/SpecialRequests/*/; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  d="${d%/}"
  b="$(basename "$d")"
  case "$b" in
    .claude|_tools|_DRIVE|token-dashboard|*_OLD_merged*) continue ;;
  esac
  # never descend into a symlink (the Drive link)
  [ -L "$d" ] && continue
  candidates+=("$d")
done
candidates+=("$DEV")

classify() {
  d="$1"
  b="${d#$HOME/DEV/}"
  if [ ! -d "$d/.git" ]; then
    top="$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
    if [ -z "$top" ]; then
      echo "NOTREPO|$b|-|-|-"
    else
      echo "NESTED|$b|${top#$HOME/}|-|-"
    fi
    return
  fi
  remote="$(git -C "$d" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -z "$remote" ]; then
    dirty=$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    echo "NOREMOTE|$b|-|$dirty|-"
    return
  fi
  git -C "$d" fetch origin --quiet 2>/dev/null
  dirty=$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  br="$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)"
  counts="$(git -C "$d" rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{u} 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -z "$counts" ]; then
    echo "REPO|$b|$br|$dirty|noupstream"
  else
    ahead=$(echo "$counts" | awk '{print $1}')
    behind=$(echo "$counts" | awk '{print $2}')
    echo "REPO|$b|$br|$dirty|${ahead}a/${behind}b"
  fi
}
export -f classify
export HOME

printf '%s\n' "${candidates[@]}" | xargs -P 8 -I{} bash -c 'classify "$@"' _ {} >> "$OUT"
echo "walked: $(wc -l < "$OUT")"

===== docs/STATUS.md
# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-09-19: project created. Holds the global TypeSafe key installer and a smoke test.
- TypeSafe skill installed in Claude Code as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7 (user scope).
- Key storage decided: macOS Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, exported by `~/.zshenv`.
  Chosen over a plaintext `.env` because `machine.macos.md` says secrets live in the Keychain,
  and because the `.zshenv` line contains no secret and is safe to commit.

## Next
- On the Mac: run `./setup_global_key.sh` in Terminal.app, restart Claude Code, run `python smoke_test.py`.
- Windows is not covered yet. Git Bash would need `~/.bashrc` and PowerShell `$PROFILE`
  reading from Credential Manager or DPAPI. Not built.

## Open questions
- Whether any real Baylor workflow wants System One judgments. Nothing committed yet.

## Gotchas
- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
- Claude Code must be restarted after the installer runs. A running session keeps the
  environment it started with.

===== AGENTS.md (first 60 lines)
# AGENTS.md

Project: TypeSafe_Sandbox

## What this is
A sandbox for building against the TypeSafe System One API (the Jev model), which
returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo. It lives in the macOS Keychain and is exported globally by
`~/.zshenv`; `setup_global_key.sh` installs that once per machine. `smoke_test.py`
proves the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

## Secrets
- Never paste the API key into a chat session. Claude Code transcripts under
  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.
- Never put the key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`. Both are tracked.
- The key has one home per machine: the macOS Keychain, service name `typesafe-api-key`.

"""Prove the global TypeSafe API key resolves and the System One API answers.

There is deliberately no python-dotenv here. The key is meant to be available
globally from the environment (macOS Keychain -> ~/.zshenv -> every zsh), so
reading anything other than os.environ would hide a broken setup.

Run:  python smoke_test.py
"""

import os
import sys

REQUIRED_VAR = "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"


def require_key() -> None:
    if os.environ.get(REQUIRED_VAR):
        return
    print(f"{REQUIRED_VAR} is not set in this environment.\n", file=sys.stderr)
    print("Fix it in this order:", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  1. Run ./setup_global_key.sh in Terminal.app (not through Claude Code).", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  2. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it", file=sys.stderr)
    print("     started with, so it will not see the new variable until restarted.", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  3. Check status any time with ./setup_global_key.sh --check", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main() -> int:
    require_key()

    try:
        from typesafe_sdk import Noul, TypeSafeClient
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        print("typesafe-sdk is not installed. Run:  pip install typesafe-sdk", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # The client picks the key up from TYPESAFE_API_KEY on its own.
    with TypeSafeClient() as client:
        response = client.system_one(
            state={"document": "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP."},
            questions={"billing": Noul(instructions="Is this ticket about billing?")},
        )

    probability = response.nouls["billing"].noul
    print(f"question: is this ticket about billing?")
    print(f"answer:   {probability}")
    print()
    print("The key resolved from the environment and the API answered. Setup is working.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

-rw-r--r--@ 1 kristinarash  staff  4413 Sep 19 09:23 setup_global_key.sh
=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the TypeSafe API key once, globally, on macOS.
#
# The key goes into the macOS Keychain (service: typesafe-api-key). A line added to
# ~/.zshenv exports it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY for every zsh, including the
# non-interactive shells Claude Code spawns. That line holds no secret, so it is
# safe even if your dotfiles are in a git repo.
#
# Run this in Terminal.app, NOT through Claude Code. The prompt needs a real
# terminal, and anything typed into a Claude session is written to a transcript
# that is tracked in the dotclaude repo.
#
# Usage:  ./setup_global_key.sh          install or update the key
#         ./setup_global_key.sh --check  report status, change nothing

set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="typesafe-api-key"
ZSHENV="$HOME/.zshenv"
MARKER="# >>> typesafe api key >>>"

if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
  echo "This installer is macOS only (it uses the Keychain). See docs/STATUS.md for Windows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

keychain_has_key() {
  security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w >/dev/null 2>&1
}

zshenv_has_block() {
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && grep -qF "$MARKER" "$ZSHENV"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
  keychain_has_key && echo "keychain:  key present (service $SERVICE)" || echo "keychain:  MISSING"
  zshenv_has_block && echo "zshenv:    export block present" || echo "zshenv:    MISSING"
  # Never interpolate the value itself: ${VAR:-default} expands to the VALUE when set.
  if [[ -n "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
    echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set (${#TYPESAFE_API_KEY} characters)"
  else
    echo "this shell: TYPESAFE_API_KEY is NOT SET"
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# --- 1. get the key, without it ever reaching a screen, a log, or shell history ---
if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no terminal on stdin." >&2
  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if keychain_has_key; then
  echo "A key is already in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."
  printf "Replace it? [y/N] "
  read -r reply
  [[ "$reply" == [yY] ]] || { echo "Left the existing key alone."; exit 0; }
fi

printf "Paste your TypeSafe API key (input is hidden, from https://console.typesafe.ai/): "
IFS= read -rs API_KEY
printf "\n"

if [[ -z "${API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: empty input, nothing written." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -A allows any process running as you to read the item with no GUI prompt. Without
# it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang the shell.
# -U updates the item if it already exists.
security add-generic-password \
  -a "$USER" \
  -s "$SERVICE" \
  -l "TypeSafe API key" \
  -D "application password" \
  -j "Used by TYPESAFE_API_KEY, exported from ~/.zshenv" \
  -w "$API_KEY" \
  -A -U
unset API_KEY
echo "Stored in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."

# --- 2. export it from ~/.zshenv, idempotently ---
# .zshenv, not .zshrc: only .zshenv is sourced for non-interactive shells, which is
# what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
if zshenv_has_block; then
  echo "~/.zshenv already has the export block, leaving it as is."
else
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && cp "$ZSHENV" "$ZSHENV.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
  cat >> "$ZSHENV" <<'BLOCK'

# >>> typesafe api key >>>
# Reads from the macOS Keychain. Contains no secret, safe to commit.
# The guard means the `security` call runs once per process tree, not per subshell.
if [ -z "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s typesafe-api-key -w 2>/dev/null)"
fi
# <<< typesafe api key <<<
BLOCK
  echo "Added the export block to ~/.zshenv (previous version backed up if it existed)."
fi

# --- 3. verify, without printing the key ---
FETCHED="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$FETCHED" ]]; then
  echo "Verified: the Keychain returns a value of ${#FETCHED} characters."
else
  echo "WARNING: could not read the key back from the Keychain." >&2
  exit 1
fi
unset FETCHED

cat <<'NEXT'

Done. Two things left, in this order:
  1. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it started with,
     so it will not see the new variable until it is restarted.
  2. Run the smoke test:  python smoke_test.py

To re-check status later:  ./setup_global_key.sh --check
NEXT

  echo "Open Terminal.app and run this script there. Do not run it through Claude Code:" >&2
  echo "the prompt cannot read input, and the key would land in a tracked transcript." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if keychain_has_key; then
  echo "A key is already in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."
  printf "Replace it? [y/N] "
  read -r reply
  [[ "$reply" == [yY] ]] || { echo "Left the existing key alone."; exit 0; }
fi

printf "Paste your TypeSafe API key (input is hidden, from https://console.typesafe.ai/): "
IFS= read -rs API_KEY
printf "\n"

if [[ -z "${API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: empty input, nothing written." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -A allows any process running as you to read the item with no GUI prompt. Without
# it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang the shell.
# -U updates the item if it already exists.
security add-generic-password \
  -a "$USER" \
  -s "$SERVICE" \
  -l "TypeSafe API key" \
  -D "application password" \
  -j "Used by TYPESAFE_API_KEY, exported from ~/.zshenv" \
  -w "$API_KEY" \
  -A -U
unset API_KEY
echo "Stored in the Keychain under service '$SERVICE'."

# --- 2. export it from ~/.zshenv, idempotently ---
# .zshenv, not .zshrc: only .zshenv is sourced for non-interactive shells, which is
# what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
if zshenv_has_block; then
  echo "~/.zshenv already has the export block, leaving it as is."
else
  [[ -f "$ZSHENV" ]] && cp "$ZSHENV" "$ZSHENV.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
  cat >> "$ZSHENV" <<'BLOCK'

# >>> typesafe api key >>>
# Reads from the macOS Keychain. Contains no secret, safe to commit.
# The guard means the `security` call runs once per process tree, not per subshell.
if [ -z "${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s typesafe-api-key -w 2>/dev/null)"
fi
# <<< typesafe api key <<<
BLOCK
  echo "Added the export block to ~/.zshenv (previous version backed up if it existed)."
fi

# --- 3. verify, without printing the key ---
FETCHED="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "$SERVICE" -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$FETCHED" ]]; then
  echo "Verified: the Keychain returns a value of ${#FETCHED} characters."
else
  echo "WARNING: could not read the key back from the Keychain." >&2
  exit 1
fi
unset FETCHED

cat <<'NEXT'

Done. Two things left, in this order:
  1. Restart Claude Code. A running session keeps the environment it started with,
     so it will not see the new variable until it is restarted.
  2. Run the smoke test:  python smoke_test.py

To re-check status later:  ./setup_global_key.sh --check
NEXT

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-09-19: project created. Holds the global TypeSafe key installer and a smoke test.
- TypeSafe skill installed in Claude Code as plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7 (user scope).
- Key storage decided: macOS Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, exported by `~/.zshenv`.
  Chosen over a plaintext `.env` because `machine.macos.md` says secrets live in the Keychain,
  and because the `.zshenv` line contains no secret and is safe to commit.
- 2026-09-19: cloned onto the Mac by dev-sync. Fixed the mode on `setup_global_key.sh`,
  which was committed 644, so `./setup_global_key.sh` failed with "permission denied".
- 2026-09-19: `.venv` built with `uv`, `typesafe-sdk==0.7.0` installed. `.venv/` is gitignored,
  so every machine builds its own.
- 2026-09-19: smoke test run on the Mac. It stops at the key guard and exits 1, which is
  correct behaviour. Nothing else is untested; the key is the only thing missing.

## Next
- On the Mac: run `./setup_global_key.sh` in Terminal.app, restart Claude Code, then run
  `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py`. Rebuild the venv first if it is gone:
  `uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python typesafe-sdk`.
- Windows is not covered yet. Git Bash would need `~/.bashrc` and PowerShell `$PROFILE`
  reading from Credential Manager or DPAPI. Not built.

## Open questions
- Whether any real Baylor workflow wants System One judgments. Nothing committed yet.

## Gotchas
- `~/.zshenv` is the right profile file, not `~/.zshrc`. Only `.zshenv` is sourced for
  non-interactive shells, which is what Claude Code's Bash tool spawns.
- `security add-generic-password -A` lets any process running as you read the item with
  no GUI prompt. Without it, a non-interactive read can raise a blocking dialog and hang
  the shell. This is the same practical threat model as a `chmod 600` file.
- Claude Code must be restarted after the installer runs. A running session keeps the
  environment it started with.

## What happened

It stopped at step 1: there is no TypeSafe key on this Mac. That is the test working correctly, not a bug. It exits 1 and tells you what to do.

The installer was saved without run permission (mode `644`). So `./setup_global_key.sh` would have failed for you with "permission denied". It is now `755`. Fixed, committed, pushed.

## What I got ready

- Built `.venv` with `uv`. Installed `typesafe-sdk 0.7.0`.
- Checked the test's code against that SDK version. `system_one(state=, questions=)`, `Noul(instructions=)` and `response.nouls[...].noul` all match. So it will not crash on an import or a renamed field.

## Your turn — 3 steps

You have to do step 1 yourself. The script refuses to run through me on purpose, so your key never lands in a saved transcript.

1. Open **Terminal.app** and run:
   ```
   cd ~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && ./setup_global_key.sh
   ```
2. Restart Claude Code.
3. Back in **Terminal.app**, run:
   ```
   cd ~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && .venv/bin/python smoke_test.py
   ```

Heads up: even after you restart Claude Code, *this* session will still not see the key. It keeps the environment it started with. That is why step 3 is in Terminal.

You said you have the key and it is on Windows. Here is what the Mac needs.

**Do not paste the key into this chat.** Chat transcripts get saved and pushed to GitHub. Type it into Terminal only.

## The short answer: 4 steps

**1. Get the key text on the Mac.**
Easiest: open `https://console.typesafe.ai/` in a Mac browser and copy your key. It is the same key for both machines.
(Or read it back on Windows, however you set it there, in a normal PowerShell window — not Claude Code.)

**2. Open Terminal.app and run:**
```
cd ~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && ./setup_global_key.sh
```
It asks you to paste the key. Your typing stays hidden. It puts the key in the Mac Keychain and adds one safe line to `~/.zshenv`.

**3. Restart Claude Code.**
A running session keeps the environment it started with. It will not see the key until you restart.

**4. Back in Terminal.app:**
```
cd ~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox && .venv/bin/python smoke_test.py
```

That is it. The Python side is already done — I built `.venv` and installed `typesafe-sdk 0.7.0`.

## Two things you should know

**I was wrong earlier.** I said this project was built on the Mac today. It was built on **Windows**. My check accidentally matched my own session log. Corrected in STATUS.md and pushed.

**The Claude Code TypeSafe plugin is not on this Mac.** Only Windows has it. The smoke test does not need it, so steps 1–4 still work. If you also want the `/typesafe` skill inside Claude Code here, run the same plugin install command you used on Windows. I did not guess it.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# 2026-09-19 — Mac dev-sync, then TypeSafe key setup on both machines

Machine: Mac (`~/DEV`). Two sessions ran today; this handoff covers both.

## What was being worked on and why

1. `/dev-sync` on the Mac, to reconcile with GitHub after Windows work on 09/17–09/18.
2. Getting the TypeSafe System One API key working, first on Windows, then on the Mac,
   so `TypeSafe_Sandbox/smoke_test.py` passes on both boxes.

## Decisions made, with the reasoning

- **`TypeSafe_Sandbox` was authored on Windows, not the Mac.** An earlier claim in this
  session that it was built on the Mac was wrong. The check that produced it grepped
  `~/.claude/projects` for the originating session id, and matched the *current* session's
  own transcript, because the id had been printed into this session's tool output.
  Discriminate with `grep -rl "<session id>" ~/.claude/projects | grep -v <this job id>`.
- **The key does not sync between machines. Each machine holds its own copy.**
  - Mac: macOS Keychain, service `typesafe-api-key`, exported by `~/.zshenv`.
  - Windows: `~/.claude/typesafe.env`, one line. Auto-gitignored by the dotclaude
    whitelist, because that `.gitignore` starts with `/*`.
- **The key needs its `apikey_` prefix.** The console shows `apikey_<36>_<64>`, 108 chars.
  Dropping the prefix returns a clean `401 authentication_error`. A malformed body returns
  `422` instead, so 401 means the key is wrong and 422 means the request is wrong. That
  split is the fastest way to tell which end is at fault. This cost the first attempt.
- **Claude Code does not need a restart for the Mac Bash tool to see the key.** The Bash
  tool spawns a fresh zsh, which sources `~/.zshenv`. A restart only matters for things
  that inherit Claude Code's own environment, such as plugin and MCP processes.
- **`TypeSafe_Sandbox` classified `personal` in the backup manifest**, matching
  `sleep-scheduler`. Eric should change it to `institutional` if a Baylor workflow adopts it.
- Conflict on `global-memory/transcripts/2026-09-17.md` resolved by **union merge, keeping
  both sides** (80 + 80 lines → 82), per the dev-sync rule for append-heavy logs.

## Files created or modified

- `~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox/setup_global_key.sh` — mode fixed 644 → 755. It had been
  committed non-executable, so `./setup_global_key.sh` failed with "permission denied".
- `~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/STATUS.md` — rewritten across both sessions.
- `~/DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox/.venv/` — built with `uv`, `typesafe-sdk==0.7.0`. Gitignored.
- `~/DEV/graphify-out/*` — nightly generated output, committed twice today.
- `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json` — added `DEV/TypeSafe_Sandbox`; now 139 paths.
- `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/2026-09-17.md` — union merged.
- `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — cleared, all entries resolved.
- `~/DEV/CLAUDE.md` — router rows for TypeSafe_Sandbox (from the other session, PR #4).

## Verified, not assumed

- `.venv/bin/python smoke_test.py` exits 0 on the Mac and returns `billing = 0.98`.
- On Windows, Noul / Choice / Score all returned sane values against the live API.
- 143 DEV repos fetched and clean. Fetch freshness confirmed by counting `FETCH_HEAD`
  files touched in the last hour, not by trusting the walk's exit code. A `git fetch`
  failing silently under `xargs` is the main way "clean" becomes a lie.

## Next actions, most important first

1. Nothing is built on TypeSafe yet. Decide whether any real Baylor workflow wants
   System One judgments. Until then the sandbox is proof-of-life only.
2. TOS evidence brief: **do not send.** Codex found 3 numeric misquotes and a bad Poisson
   argument. See `handoffs/2026-09-18-tos-evidence-review-and-ri5-002.md`.
3. Research in 5 #002 is built but not sent (PR #8).
4. Status report #3 due 9/25.

## Mid-flight / open

- TypeSafe plugin (`typesafe@typesafe-ai` v0.5.7) is installed on **Windows only**. The Mac
  has no such plugin; confirmed absent from `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`.
  The smoke test does not need it. Install on the Mac only if the `/typesafe` skill is wanted.
- Backup manifest class for `TypeSafe_Sandbox` is a guess (`personal`). Eric may override.
